messages: sam: Quick sync 3 filters + actions row4 11. Dropping a screenshot and prototype link: https://files.redwood/s/abc. Need product/eng/design alignment on: primary CTA placement, microcopy for disabled state, keyboard tab order, and toast wording. Goal: freeze for sprint. elaine: Re: mock 11 — I like the compact filters but there are 2 accessibility/UX concerns: (a) when rows are selected the main 'Approve' action is tucked into the kebab which makes it hard to discover; (b) current disabled button text 'Approve' is ambiguous. Suggestion: surface a small floating action bar with a count chip + explicit verb. jon: Floating bar is doable. Implementation notes: - Make the bar position: sticky at bottom of list container to avoid pushing surrounding content. - Only render when selectionCount > 0 to keep DOM light. - First focusable element should be the count chip so keyboard users land there before the CTA. jon: Example aria snippet (will iterate): <div role="status" aria-live="polite">3 selected</div> <button id="approve" aria-disabled="false">Approve selected results</button> aria: A11y checklist: - DOM/tab order must reflect: filter controls -> list items -> floating action bar. If actions are before the list in DOM, keyboard users will miss results. - Button text: "Approve selected results" > "Approve 3" for clarity. Shorten later when we have metrics. - Disabled state copy: "Select results to approve" — more instructive than a disabled verb. - Contrast: disabled button color fails WCAG 4.5:1 on 12px text. Either increase contrast or bump size to 14px. - Announcements: use aria-live="assertive" for the completion toast: "3 results approved". sam: My take: prioritize clarity this iteration. Decisions: 1) CTA copy when enabled: "Approve selected results". 2) CTA copy when none selected: "Select results to approve" (disabled). 3) Floating/sticky action bar appears on selection with a visible focus ring; first tabbable = count chip; then the Approve button. 4) Toast text: "{n} results approved" with aria-live assertive. elaine: I'll update the Figma with: - compact filters row retained - floating bar layout + count chip treatment - focus ring styles and keyboard flow overlays - accessible color tokens for disabled state (targeting 4.5:1) ETA: EOD. jon: I'll prototype the sticky bar and test for layout jank. If we can animate opacity without shifting layout that's ideal. aria: I'll draft a one-page a11y QA checklist (keyboard flow, screen reader announce tests, color contrast validations) and run it against the updated mock. upload-bot: uploaded files: filters_actions_v3.png, floating_bar_prototype.html (https://files.redwood/s/abc) sam: Thanks. Action owners: @elaine mocks, @jon prototype spike, @aria a11y checklist. If blockers show up, flag before sprint planning tomorrow. :thumbsup:
